title: Settings password
detail: Needed to weaken anything. Best typed by someone else, or written down away from the computer.

title: No weakening during active locks
detail: While anything is locked, no setting (strict mode included) can be weakened.

title: Tamper protection
detail: Clock changes, task managers, private windows and Tor, unsupported browsers. Off: task-managers, private, unsupported-browsers.
command: kc9k tamper task-managers on; kc9k tamper private on; kc9k tamper unsupported-browsers on

title: Strict mode
detail: While anything is locked: no sudo or pkexec, no root login or su to root, nothing runs from /home or /tmp, no containers or virtual machines.

title: Strict mode's own lock
detail: Keeps strict mode switched on even while nothing else is locked.

title: No root password
detail: Can't read /etc/shadow (run as root to check).

title: Installer media guard
detail: While anything is locked: operating system and USB writer download pages blocked, image writers and Disks closed.

title: Firmware lock
detail: This computer's firmware can't be changed from Linux. Do it in the firmware's own setup (press F2, F1, F10 or Del while the computer starts): turn off booting from USB and the network, lock the boot order, and set a firmware (setup) password that a trusted person types and keeps.

title: No-escape
detail: Last: kc9k.nofreeze and recovery mode stop working, and the boot menu gets a password nobody knows. Until then they are the way out of a bug (R-ESCAPE-1); try it in a virtual machine first.
